verification_report.summary:
The four named lemmas, the common-barrier capacity criterion, and the dominated-continuity corollary pass under the explicitly accepted local inputs and audited dependencies. The strict verdict for the entire supplied section is wrong solely because its standalone monotone-sequence observation omits a necessary hypothesis on decreasing limits. This does not invalidate the main criterion or its removal of the total-mass assumption.

Fixed-measure exponential convergence follows from the stipulated local Cegrell input, chart corrections, the exponential curvature bound, and the arbitrary-subsequence criterion. The mixed-product expansion gives uniform capacity domination for a common bounded range without BMP. The moving-product proof has the correct factorization, all four Stokes terms, and the correct signs and factor 1/2 in the energy identity. Both smooth torsion types are controlled; the gradient estimates are uniform in j and l. Exact-background decreasing approximation and accepted bounded continuity justify the nonsmooth passage. Fixing a sufficiently large l before sending j to infinity closes the quantifiers.

Weighted lower semicontinuity is valid for extended measures of possibly infinite mass. At each fixed cutoff, locality and bounded capacity continuity apply to the moving quasi-continuous weights. Positivity bounds that integral by the untruncated integral; monotone convergence then removes the cutoff. Consequently both rooftop limit passages are justified without uniform total mass or subtraction of infinite measures.

The explicit barrier phi-C makes every relevant envelope and monotone limit genuine. Finite contact partitions give the summable self-error estimate. The zero weighted integral implies vanishing measure on {p<u}, and P_{delta theta}(phi)-C supplies the smaller-background competitor needed for strict domination with coefficient zero. Ordinary singularity equivalence follows directly from the barriers; no envelope-class closure or model fixed-point condition is assumed. The final sandwich and arbitrary-subsequence argument give capacity convergence.

Both domination regimes supply the self-error convergence, uniform finite masses, and uniformly vanishing raw tails through sublevels of the fixed barrier. The audited raw-tail theorem then proves finiteness of the limiting measure and raw weak convergence. No BMP, PVP, or uniform positive lower mass is used.

The extraction statement and the two displayed source omissions were checked directly in [KN22 v1, Lemmas 2.1–2.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.11550v1). The ordinary-type scope and the additional mass hypothesis of the source criterion were compared with [ALS26 v1, Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.02339v1); neither global result was imported. The GZ17 section location was corroborated by the publisher's contents, but its full chapter was not directly inspected; the local convergence input remains expressly conditional.

critical_errors.location: Monotone capacity observation immediately after Weighted lower semicontinuity
critical_errors.issue: The assertion that a genuine monotone sequence with a common upper bound has a genuine common lower bound is false for decreasing sequences unless the limit is also assumed genuine (or a genuine lower barrier is already known). For theta>=0, v_j identically -j consists of genuine theta-psh potentials and has common upper bound 0, but its limit is identically -infinity; any function below every v_j is identically -infinity. Thus the stated hypotheses do not justify the proposed lower bound or its deep-sublevel capacity decay. This is a standalone overstatement: the actual rooftop and upper-tail sequences in the criterion have the explicit lower barrier phi-C, so their monotone passages and the mass-free criterion are valid.

repair_hints: Replace the monotone observation by: 'A decreasing sequence with a genuine limit has that limit as a common lower bound. An increasing sequence of genuine potentials with a common upper bound has its first term as a common lower bound and a genuine canonical limit. More generally, a fixed genuine lower barrier excludes collapse in the decreasing case.' Explicitly note that phi-C supplies this barrier for every monotone sequence used in the capacity criterion. The existing truncation proof then applies. No total-mass hypothesis or change to the main theorem or corollary is needed.
